# /repair-page

## Purpose

Fix a page that failed review without losing the evidence and without
rolling the dice again. A repair states exactly what has to change and
what must stay as it is, produces a new version beside the failed one, and
is finished only when someone has opened the new file and seen each change
in it. Repairs are counted. When the count reaches the project's limit the
command stops generating and sends the work back to the plan or the
references, where the cause usually is.

## Use When

- A review has verdict `flagged` and its open findings can be fixed in the
  image.
- A repaired version came back with some of the requested changes undone.
- `/continuity-review` added a finding to a page that had passed.

## Inputs

- `render` (ID, required): the flagged render, e.g. `PG_001_002_V01`. A page
  ID selects its `current_render`, or its newest render when the page is
  still at `rendered`.
- `findings` (list of `F##`, optional, default every `open` finding of the
  review): which findings this request addresses.
- `provider` (string, optional, default the provider of the failed render):
  needs `capabilities.imageEditing` to take an edit target.
- `--live` (flag, optional, default off): call the provider after the cost
  confirmation. Without it the run is a dry run.

## Invokes Agents

- visual-reviewer
- prompt-director
- image-generation-specialist

## Required Skills

- page-repair
- prompt-compilation
- pixel-review

## Process

1. Read `reviews/<RENDER_ID>.review.yaml` and `repair_policy.max_cycles`
   in `project.yaml` (default 2). If the review's `repair_cycle` has
   already reached the limit, stop. Request no further generation for the
   page, record the upstream issue and the decision needed, and return to
   `/page-plan`, `/panel-ledger`, `/character-bible`, or
   `/visual-development`.
2. Mark the failed version superseded and keep it. Its file stays in
   `renders/`, its review keeps the verdict `flagged`, and its generation
   record takes `status: rejected`. Nothing is deleted or written over,
   and the page does not list it as the result once the replacement is
   reviewed.
3. Find the cause of each finding. Some are in the image alone. Others come
   from upstream ambiguity: a character with no identity sheet, two
   characters the bible does not tell apart, a ledger row that never said
   who holds the object, a position with no landmark. Fix an upstream cause
   first, in the bible, the page file, or the reference plan. Sending the
   same ambiguous description again repeats the failure.
4. State the repair in four parts: the edit target (the exact render), the
   failing panels with their finding IDs, the exact changes, and the locked
   elements. Write each change so its presence can be seen in the result
   ("Give Oskar a round face and a hooded jacket in panel 3"). Lock
   everything that was right: lettering, panel borders, the characters who
   passed.
5. Keep identity repairs apart from prop and state repairs when a combined
   request has left some changes undone. Send the identity findings in one
   request and the prop or state findings in another, each with the
   reference sheet of what it corrects attached.
6. prompt-director compiles the request: `node scripts/compile-prompts.js
   --page <page.yaml> --provider <id> --repair <review.yaml>`. The package
   has `mode: repair`, `edit_target`, and a `repair` block with
   `of_render`, `findings`, `changes`, and `locked`. A provider without
   `imageEditing` cannot take an edit target; the repair is then a full
   regeneration from the corrected plan, still saved as the next version.
7. Cost gate: a repair run is its own batch. Show the estimate and wait
   for confirmation. Run `node scripts/generate-assets.js --page
   <page.yaml> --provider <id>` for the dry run and add `--live --yes`
   after the user confirms.
8. Save the result as a sibling version with the next number (`V02` after
   `V01`) and complete its generation record, with unreported metadata
   recorded as unavailable.
9. Reopen the new file. Verify each requested change, one by one, in the
   pixels. A successful edit call is not evidence of a repair. A change
   that did not happen leaves its finding `open`.
10. Recheck the whole page and its neighbors. Fill all fourteen checks
    again on the new render and look for collateral changes to text,
    identities, anatomy, clothing, and geography, here and against the
    current renders of the previous and next pages. The visual-reviewer
    who rechecks did not generate the version.
11. Write `reviews/<NEW_RENDER_ID>.review.yaml`: `supersedes` names the old
    render, `repair_cycle` is the old value plus one, and each repaired
    finding has `status: fixed` with a `recheck` (`render`, `evidence`).
    The verdict is `fixed` when no blocking finding is open, `flagged`
    otherwise. On `fixed`, move `current_render` in `page.yaml` to the new
    version and set `status: reviewed`.
12. If the verdict is still `flagged` and cycles remain, run the command
    again on the new render. If the limit is reached, stop as in step 1.
    Do not raise the limit and do not declare success.
13. Run `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root production --issue
    <ISS_ID>` and the self-evaluation gates on the new review. Report what
    was repaired, what was rechecked and seen, what is still open, and
    which later pages used the failed render as a reference and need
    another review.

## Outputs

- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/renders/<PG_ID>_V##.png`, the
  sibling version; earlier versions stay on disk.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/prompts/<provider>.yaml`, the
  repair package (`mode: repair`); validates against
  `schemas/prompt-package.schema.json`.
- `production/generations/<PG_ID>/GEN_<PG_ID>_<attempt##>.yaml`, validates
  against `schemas/generation-record.schema.json`.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/reviews/<RENDER_ID>.review.yaml`
  for the new render; validates against
  `schemas/visual-review.schema.json`.
- `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`, with
  `current_render` moved after a `fixed` verdict (`schemas/page.schema.json`).

## Notes

- Cost warning: every repair request is a generation. Dry run is the
  default and each repair run needs its own confirmation.
- `validate-workspace.js` rejects a review whose `repair_cycle` exceeds
  `repair_policy.max_cycles`, a `fixed` finding without recheck evidence,
  and a `fixed` verdict with an open blocking finding. Changing
  `max_cycles` is a project decision for the user.
- After the plan or the references have been corrected, the page starts
  again through `/generate-pages` as a first render of the revised plan,
  with a new version number.
- A lettering error on an in-image page is repaired here with the art
  locked. In overlay mode it is fixed in `lettering.yaml` through
  `/lettering`, with no generation at all.
- Local edits move things nobody asked to move. That is why the recheck
  covers the whole page and its neighbors and never the edited panel
  alone.
- Related: `/visual-review` (writes the findings), `/generate-pages`
  (first renders), `/reference-plan` and `/panel-ledger` (upstream fixes),
  `rules/common/repair-limits.md` (the policy).
